To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a SELEX protocol was modified in order to evolve ssDNA biotemplates for gold nanoparticle synthesis and that the resulting pool of ssDNA biotemplate sequences produced colloidal gold solutions with distinct absorbance spectra compared to the starting pool of sequences.
a modified SELEX protocol was used to evolve imidazole modified sequences that mediate nanoparticle formation and the resulting pool of sequences had conserved base motifs.
the SELEX process was successfully adapted to evolve a randomized pool of imimazole modified ssDNA towards sequences that meditate the formation of gold nanoparticle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a modified SELEX protocol to identify biotemplates that are able to form nanoparticles in aqueous solution and the analysis of the sequences isolated by our protocol.
the development of a SELEX protocol for the identification of ssDNA sequences that mediate nanoparticle synthesis.
the evolution of DNA sequences towards sequences that can be used as biotemplates for the synthesis of nanoparticles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this SELEX protocol was successful in evolving ssDNA sequences that mediate nanoparticle formation in a base-specific manner.
the evolved pool has been shown to contain sequences that mediate gold nanoparticle formation from Au3+ ions.
the SELEX protocol developed in this project was able to evolve a randomized pool of imadazole modified ssDNA towards sequences that bind gold atoms and mediate the formation nanoparticles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a modified ssDNA SELEXTM was developed in order that a pool of imidazol modified ssDNA sequences could be evolved towards sequences that mediat the formation of Au nanoparticles from aqueous Au3+ precursor.
a SELEX based protocol was developed to evolve a library of imidazoles towards sequences that mediated the formation of gold colloids from aqueous gold precursors.

we developed an ssDNA SELEX method that can be used for the evolution of ssDNA sequences that bind to nanoparticles and that we have identified conserved motifs that are likely to be involved in nanoparticle binding.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SELEX can be modified to evolve ssDNA sequences that can mediate the formation and/or stabilization of nanoparticles in aqueous solution.
a SELEX-like approach could be used to evolve biotemplates for the formation of nanoparticles of different materials.
